name: Seattle Farmers Markets
_operators: Two organisations run Seattle's markets and this list spans both. Neighborhood Farmers Markets (seattlefarmersmarkets.org) runs Ballard, U District, Capitol Hill, West Seattle, Columbia City, Lake City, Phinney, Magnolia and Queen Anne. The Seattle Farmers Market Association (sfmamarkets.com) runs five, of which Wallingford was already here under the other operator's name; Central District, Madison Park and South Lake Union were missing entirely until 2026-08-12. A curated city list only stays complete if somebody re-reads the operators' own market lists, so when auditing Seattle, enumerate BOTH sitemaps rather than trusting this array.

name: Seattle Local Markets
_source: https://www.seattlelocalmarkets.com/calendar, read 2026-08-24. The page is Squarespace but NOT a Squarespace Events collection - collection type 10, a plain page whose calendar is hand-typed HTML text blocks with no <article>, no dates= export link and no coordinate anywhere. mapsee_ingest_squarespace.py reads 0 events from it, which is why this is a curated inline source rather than a line in squarespace_sources.json.
_cadence: Two of the three are MONTHLY, which is what the `nth` field was added for. The operator publishes both the rule and the enumerated dates, and the two agree exactly: Fremont's seven 2026 dates are every last Thursday (April 30, May 28, June 25, July 30, August 27, September 24, October 29 - note the alternation between the fourth Thursday and the fifth, which is why the rule is 'last' and not 'fifth'), and Magnolia Flea's are every second Saturday (April 11 through October 10). The RULE is recorded here rather than the date list because a rule survives into 2027 and a frozen list does not. test_ingest_markets.py pins both against the operator's own published dates.
_seasons_end_where_the_page_does: The page says 'November & December 2026 Dates TBD!' for both dated markets, and footnotes that dates get altered to accommodate the holiday season. So season_end is the last date the operator has actually published, not the end of the year: projecting the rule to November 26 - last Thursday, US Thanksgiving - is exactly the well-formed, plausible, wrong pin that footnote is warning about. Re-read the page in the autumn and extend.

markets.name: Fremont Evening Market
markets._hours_are_seasonal: The page gives two sets: 4-8 in the WINTER season and 5-9 in spring, summer and fall. Every published 2026 date falls in April-October, so 5-9 is the only one of the two that can ever apply to a date this entry emits. If November/December dates are published, they need their own entry at 4-8 rather than an edit to this one.
markets._placement: The page locates it as 'N 35th St between Triangle & El Camino in Fremont' - a street market with no house number and no coordinate published. Pinned at the midpoint of the two named businesses, both of which are in OSM: Triangle Spirits (3507 Fremont Pl N, 47.6508151,-122.3508326) and El Camino (607 N 35th St, 47.6505296,-122.3509101). They are ~35m apart, so the block is short and the midpoint is honest to it. coords_exact is deliberately NOT set: this is a block, not a door.

markets.name: Magnolia Flea Market
markets._placement: OSM carries the building as shop=antiques 'Magnolia Vintage Warehouse & Flea Market' at this exact point, so this is a surveyed door rather than a geocode - hence coords_exact, which opts the row out of the Census re-lookup in mapsee_supabase_sync. It also costs nothing from the geocode budget.

markets.name: Magnolia Vintage Warehouse
markets._is_this_a_market_or_a_shop: OSM tags it shop=antiques, and this adapter's own Overpass loader drops any marketplace open more than _OSM_MAX_DAYS (3) days a week as a shop rather than a market day. 'Open each and every weekend' is two days, inside that line, and the operator lists it on its own market calendar alongside the other two - so it is kept, by the same rule the OSM loader applies. It shares an address with Magnolia Flea Market and both emit on second Saturdays; that is the source's own claim rather than a duplicate - the flea market is the event, this is the venue's ordinary weekend opening - and they stay distinct through mapsee_dedupe_events.py because the names differ.
markets._no_season: The page gives none: 'Open Each and Every Weekend' with no range. So none is recorded here. See the SFMA note in the source above for why a guessed season_end is worse than no season_end.

name: OpenStreetMap Marketplaces
_run_weekdays: Monday AND Thursday. This is 245 Overpass calls at roughly 45s each - over three hours - so it must not run daily, and it now runs as its OWN workflow job (markets_osm) with its own store, its own sync and a 330-minute budget. That isolation is the load-bearing part: until 2026-08-17 the sweep ran inside the `feeds` job, and on Monday 2026-08-17 it hit that job's 240-minute ceiling MID-STEP - so the checkpoint sync never ran and the day delivered nothing at all, including the Socrata and ICS work that had already succeeded and the twenty sources queued behind it. The Saturday and Sunday either side took 52 and 55 minutes, because run_weekdays keeps this sweep to Mondays: it does not merely get LOST to the timeout, it CAUSES it. Two days rather than one because a source with a single weekly window has no retry - the 2026-08-10 run was lost the same way - and now that a failure here costs only this job, the second day is cheap.
_brazil: Added 2026-08-28. A feira livre is a weekly street market and Brazil maps them: 90 amenity=marketplace elements in the Rio box and 94 in Brasília's, comparable with the densest European cities already here. They arrive with surveyed coordinates, which is what makes them usable at all — the only geocoder in this pipeline is US Census.
